It's more like "America loses Billions to save Millions".

I'm by no means an expert but I have some knowledge in this field. The problem with the current system of hiring government contractors that was nowhere mentioned in this article is the cost plus policy that many use. So for every dollar they spend there is a small percentage tacked on as a profit for the company. So when a company bids to get a government contract they bid at one price than crank up the costs on the back end with change orders. Also when it comes to security and PMC contracts the notion that the more you spend the more you make is still very prevalent. Say what you want about blackwater/exec services but one of the reasons that they were used so readily during the height of the Iraq/Afgan conflict was they offered flat rate contracts. The difference is that if their equipment is damaged/destroyed this would eat into their bottom line. As opposed to some other companies that when equipment was destroyed they would purchase the new equipment apply a designated percentage to the sticker price and then send that bill off to the DOD.
